messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: paging: High 5xx rate detected from gateway-nyc -> backend-fanout (5m spike). Alert: gateway.5xx.rate > 2% for 5m. Escalation: paging on-call
maya: picking this up (on-call). on it.
sam: I see throttling on the fanout path, queue length climbing on edge-proxy. digging into logs now.
dmitri: putting quick context — we pushed route-split change ~30m ago (canary) that increases fanout to legacy-search. could be related.
rachel: support report — a few customers in EU are seeing search failures, some 502s surfaced to them. sending quick list.
maya: @sam can you confirm if it's a backend timeout (504) or 502 error? I see both in the spike.
sam: majority are 502 from backend 10.7.3.21 and timeouts from 10.7.3.22. throwing a query to telemetry: `sum(rate(gateway_5xx[5m])) by (backend)`
sam: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-14T23:12:05Z ERROR gateway request_id=abc123 backend=10.7.3.21 status=502 upstream_error=ETIMEDOUT
2026-03-14T23:12:06Z WARN proxy queue_len=189 target=legacy-search latency_ms=1200
```
dmitri: that aligns w/ the canary. I recommend immediate traffic isolation: rollback route-split or mark legacy-search unhealthy in router.
maya: agreed. quick mitigation: abort the canary traffic and revert split to previous traffic allocation.
maya: @deploy-bot can we rollback the canary for route:search-split? if not, freeze traffic to zero.
deploy-bot: Received rollback request: route=search-split, target=stable, user=maya — initiating.
sam: doing a traffic drain on 10.7.3.21/22. setting circuit-breaker on legacy-search with req_per_sec threshold = 50.
dmitri: also toggling autoscale delta to +0 to prevent new cold starts; looks like pods are thrashing.
rachel: customer updates: posting a short incident note to affected customer list: "We're investigating elevated errors for search; mitigation underway." pending approval.
maya: @rachel please include the ETA = 15m and note that we're rolling back a recent routing change. link: https://telemetry.internal/graphs/abc
sre-lead: +1. keep me posted. if rollback fails, fallback plan = route to cached-search variant (read-only) and notify product.
sam: rollback succeeded. traffic back to stable allocation. 5xx rate trending down.
incident-bot: Alert resolved: gateway.5xx.rate back below threshold for 3m. Closing page.
maya: seeing errors drop but a few stragglers. need postmortem and runbook update: runbook currently assumes backend flakiness, but doesn't include guidance for canary rollback or traffic isolation.
dmitri: opening a quick hotfix PR to add a guard in deploy pipeline that enforces gradual ramp with circuit-breaker if fanout count > 8. PR: https://git.internal/pr/4132
sam: action items: 
- hotfix: enforce ramp/circuit-breaker in router (owner: dmitri, PR 4132)
- runbook: add section "Canary fanout rollback" (owner: maya)
- alert tuning: increase cardinality on gateway.5xx alerts to include route and backend to avoid noisy pages (owner: sam)
- customer comms: follow-up email + postmortem summary (owner: rachel)

maya: assigning owners and due times. I'll own coordinating the postmortem doc and runbook update, due EOD.
dmitri: I'll merge PR after tests pass, target hotfix deploy in next 30m.
sam: I will update alert query to `sum by(route,backend)(rate(gateway_5xx[2m]))` and add a 1% 2m threshold as a warning, 2.5% 5m as critical.
rachel: I'll draft customer note and include bullet about rollback and expected follow-up. sending draft in #customer-notices in 45m.
maya: telemetry check: tokenized view — latency and error breakdown. link: https://telemetry.internal/dash/xyz. put a retention marker: save traces from 23:00-23:30 UTC for the postmortem.
sam: log retention set. also adding a short-lived debug endpoint to fetch proxy queue lengths: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://edge.internal/debug/queues`
maya: quick retrospective: what went wrong: missing route-level fanout guard during canary and alerting lacked route-level context. mitigations are the action items above.
sre-lead: agree. also add a periodic canary audit to infra runbook — verify fanout and backend multiplicity before canary ramp.
maya: I'll update the incident timeline in the postmortem: initial alert at 23:12, rollback at 23:18, alert resolved 23:22. link to postmortem draft: https://docs.internal/incidents/2180005555-draft
dmitri: note for follow-up: check client timeouts and backpressure behavior — proxy should reject early instead of letting upstream queue.
sam: leaving a TODO: tune route-level circuit-breaker thresholds per workload (batch vs interactive). adding to infra backlog.
rachel: customer comm sent at 00:05 UTC; customers acknowledged. will add quotes to postmortem.
maya: closing the immediate paging. follow-ups as listed. if anything spikes again re-paging on-call chain.
incident-bot: Log: incident 2180005555 transitioned to MONITORING. Participants: maya, sam, dmitri, rachel. Record created."
